name: Used Future
origin: Star Wars production design (1977) & UK comics
geography: global SF film and game design
era: post-2001: A Space Odyssey grit revolution
summary: Spaceships with mud on the tires: dents, grease, and cobbled panels.
description: "Used future" names the science-fiction look in which spaceships are work vehicles, not miracles: the Millennium Falcon's worn hull, Alien's Nostromo break-room, blade-runner drizzle — surfaces dented, duct-taped and grease-streaked, sets dressed like long-serving machinery. The look crystallized as a rebuke to gleaming-thryptic futures (2001, Star Trek bridge gloss): modelmakers (Industrial Light & Magic), production designers (Roger Christian's "used universe" brief for Star Wars) and art directors built grime into hero props. Games (Outer Wilds, Hardspace: Shipbreaker) and shows (The Expanse, Andor) inherit it: the future as blue-collar workplace.
culturalContext: "Used future" reframed science fiction as workplace: Star Wars' worn hulls and Alien's break-rooms answered the gleaming 2001 future with blue-collar grit, and The Expanse, Andor and Hardspace: Shipbreaker inherit the doctrine — the future as labor, not miracle.

typography.notes: every surface has a service record
